paper.title_en: Microscopic Approach to Neutron Elastic and Inelastic Cross Sections
paper.abstract_en: Depending on the nuclei involved and the beam energies, reaction timescales differ tremendously. Today, distinct models are often used to describe each timescale, relying on phenomenological inputs, such as level densities or partial-widths, which limits their predictive power. This work aims to address this issue by providing a unified description of low-energy neutron elastic and inelastic reaction channels starting from microscopic predictions of the structure of mid-mass nuclei. The goal is to build a framework that is general enough to span the different reaction regimes while remaining anchored in microscopic theory. For illustration purposes, this work focuses on reactions $n+^{20}$Ne to the elastic and inelastic channels. The S-matrix is build from shell model predictions of resonances states and their spectroscopic amplitudes for $^{21}$Ne, using two different approximations of the single-particle asymptotics. Then, the shell-model predictions for the level density and single-particle partial widths are analyzed and the final cross sections are compared with evaluated ones. This method qualitatively reproduces the ENDF evaluation for the $^{20}$Ne$(n,el)$ and $^{20}$Ne$(n,n')$ cross sections. The present study also compares the Shannon entropy obtained from this model to the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE). In the future, the framework will be extended to include more complex reaction channels, such as two-nucleon and gamma channels, enabling more accurate predictions of neutron-induced reactions such as those of astrophysical interest.
